limitations: Differences in physiological, cognitive, and emotional measures due to the virtual nature of the study compared to a physical environment.
Participants' unfamiliarity with virtual reality equipment potentially affected physiological measurements and survey responses.
Uncontrolled environmental variables (humidity, temperature, daylighting) across various study locations.
Potential influence of communications between participants on expectations and survey responses.
Study typically carried out in the evenings, limiting observation of physiological fluctuations throughout the day.
Simple virtual simulation of a classroom with no interactive components, preventing participants from actively demonstrating confidence in controlling students.
Short exposure duration (between five and ten minutes) in each virtual environment, potentially limiting full adaptation to the space.
minimum_safe_summary: This empirical study investigated the effects of lighting color temperature (warm vs. cool tone) in virtual early childhood classrooms on educators' cognitive load, physiological measurements, self-efficacy, and emotions. Using a virtual reality headset, 30 participants experienced both warm (3000K CCT) and cool (4100K CCT) tone environments while completing a lesson plan. The study found that cool tone lighting significantly decreased perceived cognitive load (mental demand, difficulty, insecurity/stress) and normalized heart rates, while increasing feelings of successfulness and positive emotions (happy, calm, excited, awake) and decreasing discomfort. Furthermore, cognitive load was significantly correlated with self-efficacy, with lower cognitive load associated with higher self-efficacy. However, only weak correlations were found between physiological measurements and satisfaction or intent to spend time in the environment, leading to a failure to reject the null hypothesis for this relationship. Limitations include the virtual nature of the study, uncontrolled environmental variables across different study locations, potential participant communication, and short exposure durations.

control_conditions: other lighting color temperatures (e.g., warm-tone, neutral)
